page: The Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-8 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by Intel x86_64 processors. It provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with multithreading enabled, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1 data cache. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous 1:8 core-to-memory allocation of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The underlying processor includes modern instruction extensions such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX matrix acceleration instructions (amx_tile and amx_int8), alongside hardware cryptographic acceleration.

Hardware provisioning does not include local disk storage or bundled GPUs, requiring non-volatile state to be maintained through detached networked storage solutions. Benchmark measurements across computational workloads show balanced mid-tier throughput, recording a PassMark CPU score of 13,039.39, a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,984.0, and a stress-ng multi-core rating of 6,753.25. Memory subsystem profiling demonstrates sustained throughput with 61.99 GB/sec read and 37.24 GB/sec write bandwidth on large blocks, scaling up to 542.3 GB/sec for cached transfers.

Across specialized operational suites, the instance demonstrates consistent middle-tier results, such as 9.89 million operations per second in Redis SET testing, 11.97 GB/sec in static web serving throughput, and a PassMark database score of 4,891.5. In contrast, parallel compression shows bottlenecks, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falling into the lower quartile, and CPU-based LLM token generation remaining constrained at 6.1 tokens per second on 7B models. The high RAM-to-CPU density offers favorable cost efficiency for memory-bound services without paying for superfluous compute cores, rendering the n4-highmem-8 well-matched for in-memory caching tiers, relational database engines, intermediate ETL stages, and memory-intensive enterprise microservices.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4-highmem-8 is an Intel x86_64 instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores) and 64.0 GB of memory, delivering an expanded 8.0 GB RAM-per-vCPU ratio. The processor architecture includes advanced vector and matrix instruction support, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. It contains no onboard GPUs and does not bundle local disk storage, relying on external network storage. Benchmark evaluations place the instance reliably within median industry percentiles, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 6,984.0, a PassMark database score of 4,891.5, and 9.89 million Redis SET operations per second. While parallel compression and CPU-based language model generation show hardware limits, its resource profile delivers solid qualitative cost efficiency for memory-dominated workloads including in-memory datastores, relational databases, analytics caching, and enterprise applications.
